sections.teaching_text:
1- Referencing Points:

- Points belong to the Geometry Tab (Parameters Tab).
- Right-click on the Point symbol or just type "Point" anywhere in the workspace.

- Reference ONE Rhino point:
Create a new "Point" component.
The Grasshopper Point is colored orange, hover over it, you will read:
- "Contains a collection of three-dimentional points": This is the description of the component. All components have a specfic description.
- "Empty Point Parameter": This is the status of the component. Currently, it is empty. Let's reference a point from Rhino!
Move to the Rhino workspace, create a new POINT, then select it inside Rhino, and move to the Grasshopper workspace, right-click on the POINT COMPONENT and select: "Set One Point".
Now, the component is used (colored white instead of orange) and the Rhino Point is marked with an X.

Hover over the used component, the status of the component says:
"One locally defined value...
Referenced Point".

Click on the Referenced Point, the X in Rhino becomes green, meaning that the Grasshopper component is activated. While not activated, the X in Rhino becomes red.

THIS METHOD OF USING COMPONENTS, HOVERING OVER THEM AND READING THEIR STATUS APPLIES TO ALL COMPONENTS IN GRASSHOPPER.
ALSO, THIS IS THE SAME WAY OTHER GEOMETRIES ARE REFENCED, SUCH AS LINES, CURVES, SURFACES, SOLIDS, MESHES...


- Reference MULTIPLE Rhino points.

Apply the same procedure as above with many points.

Hover over the Grasshopper component, it says:
"3 locally defined values...
Referenced Point
Referenced Point
Referenced Point"

sub_annotations.text:
Color Coding

- Orange: Empty
- Red: Error
- White: Enabled and Showing
- Grey with Black text: Enabled and No Preview
- Faded Grey with Faded Text: Disabled

Icon Style

The same component has two different display styles. This is a personal preference...

- Text
- Icon

- Click on "Display" and select "Draw Icons"
This Boolean toggle is just used for the purpose of showing how the Point looks like when having an error

sections.teaching_text:
2- Constructing Points & Number Generators:

- Type "Construct a Point".
- Select the option "Construct a Point".
- You see that the new component, called "Construct Point" is different from the previous "Point" component.
- This new component "Construct Point" has 3 INPUTS X, Y & Z!
- It is also white, which means that it is not empty! In other words, it includes information...
- When there are components inside Grasshopper than need inputs, sometimes Grasshopper includes standard information inside of them.
- Hover over the X & Y & Z and see what the preview shows...
In this case, the X & Y & Z have the "0.0" as standard assigned information.

- Let us customize this new Point with new parameters!

- The X & Y & Z need NUMBERS.

- There are many ways in which we can make NUMBERS in Grasshopper:

1- Number Slider:
Right-click on the Number Slider and select "Edit" and go through the different options
Pay attention to the name of the Number Slider, it automatically changes according to the input it feeds.

2- Digital Scroller:
Also gives a number, but it does not have the same options as the Number Slider.

3- Panel:
If contains only a number, the Panel can be used as a Number generator!

4- Control Knob:
A rotational Number Generator with Options.

sub_annotations.text:

- X: Default
- Y: Faint

When the Point component is selected, all wires show in green-black gradient.

concepts_taught: The X & Y & Z need NUMBERS.

sections.teaching_text:
3- Panels:

- Used to UNDERSTAND what is happening.
- Most components in Grasshopper have OUTPUTS. Those outputs can be used to connect with other components.
The Panel can be used to READ & UNDERSTAND what the OUTPUTS are giving...
concepts_taught: Used to UNDERSTAND what is happening.

sections.teaching_text:
4- Lines:

- A Line is a CONNECTION between TWO POINTS.
- In Grasshopper, the ORDER of POINTS making a LINE is VERY IMPORTANT!
- The ORDER of the POINTS defines the DIRECTION of LINE.
- In Grasshopper, any LINE represents a VECTOR with the LINE's respective DIRECTION.

Creating a new Line:
- Type "Line" anywhere inside Grasshopper's workspace.
- There are many options, choose "Line" with description "Create line between two points".
- Create a panel and connect it from the output of the Line.

sub_annotations.text:
Parametric Line!

Try to change the coordinates of the Points above (X,Y,Z)
The Line updates live as you change the points' coordinates!

This is a Parametric Line, governed by the changing parameters of the points that make the Line...

This is a very simplifed example of what Grasshopper can do...

concepts_taught: A Line is a CONNECTION between TWO POINTS.

sections.teaching_text:
5- Vectors:

- A VECTOR is a DIRECTION between two points, similar to a Line.
Because it is a DIRECTION, the ORDER in which the VECTOR is formed is very important.
- A VECTOR is NOT A GEOMETRY, rather it is used to inform a certain transformation, like MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, etc...

Creating a new Vector:
- Type "Vector" anywhere inside Grasshopper's workspace.
- There are many options, choose "Vector 2pt".
- Create a panel and connect it from the output of the Line.
- Use the previous Points to make the vector.
- Hover the cursor over the various INPUTS & OUTPUTS of the "Vector 2pt" and check out what they are.
- Currently, you cannot see the vector because it is not a geometry. However, you can still visualize it by using the "Vector Display" component.
- Sometimes, you don't need to fill all the INPUTS. It is enough that the main INPUTS that activate the component are used and the OUTPUT works.
In this example, we did not give any INPUT to the U of the "Vector 2pt".
- Also, you don't always need to use all the OUTPUTS, only the ones needed for the Definition. In this case, we used only the V output to visualize the vector.

- Use a Panel and check what the Length of the vector gives.
It is similar to the Line OUTPUT, but only a NUMBER and NOT A GEOMETRY as with the Line.

- Now try to change the coordinates of the Points again, both the Line AND the Vector update simultaneously.
concepts_taught: Use the previous Points to make the vector.

sections.teaching_text:
6- Vector De/Construction:

- A VECTOR can be "deconstructed" into its basic units, XYZ.
- A VECTOR can also be constructed with XYZ INPUTS.

- Deconstructing a Vector:
- Type "Deconstruct" and choose "Deconstruct Vector".
- Deconstruct the vector on the left.
- Type "Vector" and choose "Vector XYZ".
- Reconstruct the deconstructed vector, with the same XY as the previous vector, but without the Z.
- Use the "Vector Display" to visualize the new vector.
concepts_taught: A VECTOR can also be constructed with XYZ INPUTS.
Deconstruct the vector on the left.

sections.teaching_text:
7- Curves have the following properties:

- Control Points
- Degree
- Weight

- Draw a Curve in Rhino and follow with options.

- Type Weight and check out what it does.

- Open the Point Edit sub-tab and check out the different options.

- Try to Rebuild the drawn Curve in Rhino

- Reference the drawn Curve inside Grasshopper and check out the following components:

- "Evaluate Curve"
- "Rebuild Curve"

sub_annotations.text:
Making Lines, Polylines, Closed Polylines and Curves in Grasshopper can be done in many ways...

Assignment 1:

- Type "Line" anywhere inside the Grasshopper workspace
- Choose "Line SDL"

- Go to the "Curve" tab, then "Primitive" and choose:
- "Circle"
- "Rectangle"
- "Polygon"

- Go to the "Curve" tab, then "Spline" and choose:
- "Polyline"
- "Interpolate"

- Hover the cursor over the INPUTS and try to make new geometries from these components

- Type "Divide" anywhere inside the Grasshopper workspace
- Choose "Divide Curve"
- Try to divide the above made geometries with the "Divide Curve" component

- Go to the "Curve" tab, then "Analysis" and choose:
- "End Points"
- "Point On Curve"
- "Length"
Use these components to analyze the previously made geometries

Quick Find Components in Toolbars:

"ctrl+alt+click"
on component while holding.

Try this out with the "Rebuild Curve" component.
